heroSub: The last imperial family of Iran — photographed, written, and held with editorial care.
heroCaption: Mohammad Reza Shah and Farah Pahlavi with their child, late 1960s.
poetryLines: He stands where a century leans on a single name,
not as a ruin, but as a living measure of return.
Son of a king who modernised a nation,
grandson of the man who forged a dynasty from dust and will—
he carries neither the crown’s weight nor its abandonment,
only the long duty of remaining.
Exile is a country without borders;
he has walked it in full view of the world,
speaking of law when law was broken,
of choice when choice was taken,
of a future that does not ask permission to be free.
There is no theatre in his patience.
It is the patience of someone who has watched history
arrive late, and still held the door.
Iran is not a memory to him.
It is a pulse under the skin of every map,
a language that refuses to die in the mouth,
a people who know their own name
even when others try to rename them.
If legacy is a river, he is not its end—
he is the place where it turns,
still cold, still clear,
still moving toward the sea of what might yet be.
His Highness Reza Pahlavi:
not a portrait sealed behind glass,
but a continuity—
quiet, unbroken,
and still becoming.
